key_insight: Machine learning can identify simulated degradation mechanisms in lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but reliable prediction depends strongly on training-data coverage.
engineering_relevance: Temperature- and illumination-dependent voltage measurements could support post-fabrication diagnosis, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Compare forward surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Use a multi-label classifier to detect six degradation mechanisms from open-circuit-voltage measurements.
evidence_signal: Diagnostic macro F1 reaches 0.938 versus 0.687 for calibrated physics rules; forward-model R² falls from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, recovering to 0.995 with Latin hypercube training.
watch_item: Diagnosis is demonstrated on simulated data and fails to generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
